prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1057; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is represented by counsel, who has requested that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the vehicle is listed as an insured unit. Coverage is in force for the loss period.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. Photos from the scene and the statement from the other driver are consistent with the accident occurring as described.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection shows rear-end damage consistent with the reported impact. A few older scratches appear on the bumper cover, and it is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this collision. Referred to the appraiser for a closer review.

Entry 5: Claimant's account of the accident has remained the same in every conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement and the follow-up through counsel. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the claimant's history or the records requested to date.

Entry 6: Medical records received show the reported shoulder injury is plausible for a collision of this type. Treatment followed a usual course of physical therapy and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 7: Spoke with counsel regarding the treatment timeline and the outstanding records request. Counsel confirmed the claimant's position and agreed to provide the remaining documentation.

Entry 8: File reviewed. Liability and coverage are established, and the injury is consistent with the mechanism of loss. Remaining question is the extent of the vehicle damage attributable to this impact, which is being assessed by the appraiser.
